documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported record operational performance for FY 2025-26, achieving a peak crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity. Q4 FY26 reported gross refining margin (GRM) reached $13.75 per barrel, while full-year GRM stood at $9.2 per barrel against the Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel. The company recommended a total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year, including a final dividend of INR 54 per share. CPCL is progressing with major capex initiatives, including a Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project and retail outlet expansion. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT in FY25, operating at 99.5% of installed capacity.

guidance.claim: Management expects resilient operational and financial performance momentum to continue into the new financial year.
guidance.quote: To summarize, we continue to deliver resilient operational and financial performance and see the momentum to continue in the new financial year as well.

guidance.claim: The Board will consider a bonus share issue at an appropriate time.
guidance.quote: So we feel at the right appropriate time, even the bonus issue will also be considered by the Board and the right decision will be taken.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
guidance.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL stepped up LPG production to meet demand amid global supply uncertainties.
demand_outlook.quote: With global uncertainties affecting the availability of LPG all over the world, CPCL is happy to step up the requirement when the nation needed it.

demand_outlook.claim: There is a shortfall of motor spirit in the southern market where production is lower than demand.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand.

demand_outlook.claim: Southern market growth for other products is mostly aligned with national growth projections.
demand_outlook.quote: As far as others are concerned, we have seen the southern market to be mostly aligned to the national growth projection.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred capex of INR 856 crores during the current financial year compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project has an estimated capex of INR 1,600 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor involves a outlay of INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL estimates routine annual maintenance capex at approximately INR 500 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: The new LOBS unit will add 250 KTPA of fresh Group 2 and Group 3 capacity.
capex_expansion.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred a total CAPEX expenditure of Rs. 673 crores during FY25.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL completed the installation of 1.04 MW capacity ground-mounted and rooftop solar systems on plant area buildings.
capex_expansion.quote: 1.04 MW capacity of Ground Mounted and Roof top solar system on plant area buildings

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a Q4 FY26 GRM of $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: Core GRM for the fourth quarter was $10.3 per barrel.
CPCL incurred forex losses of approximately INR 200 crores for Q4 and INR 350 crores for the full year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL recorded a full-year GRM of $4.22 per barrel for FY25 compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL achieved a Q4 FY25 GRM of $6.22 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: Fuel and loss for FY25 reduced to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a Gross Refining Margin of $3.40 per barrel for 9M FY2024-25 compared to $8.64 per barrel in FY2023-24.
CPCL's Core Gross Refining Margin was $3.75 per barrel for 9M FY2024-25 down from $8.21 per barrel in FY2023-24.
Net operating expenditure for 9M FY2024-25 stood at Rs 945 crore compared to Rs 1,215 crore in FY2023-24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT in FY 2025-26, representing 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL processed 2.93 MMT of crude throughput in Q4 FY26, operating at 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: Annual production reached record levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel and 1.318 MMT for petrol.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: LPG production hit a record high of 447 TMT in FY 2025-26.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: Pharma-grade Hexane capacity doubled from 30 to 60.
orders_capacity.quote: It was 30, now the capacity is 60.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL recorded crude throughput of 7,480 TMT for 9M FY2024-25 compared to 11,642 TMT in FY2023-24.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL lowered its gross debt-to-equity ratio to 0.18.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings stand at INR 1,900 crores, while net borrowings stand at INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a total dividend of INR 62 per share for FY 2025-26, including an interim dividend of INR 8 and a final dividend of INR 54 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's absolute debt stood at Rs. 3,100 crores as of March 31, 2025, compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as of March 31, 2024.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share for FY25.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's net worth stood at Rs 7,491 crore as of 9M FY2024-25.
Working capital position of CPCL reached Rs 5,098 crore as of December 31, 2024.

risks_headwinds.claim: Logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility continue to pose operational challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Short-term supply disruptions affected 30% to 40% of Middle East term crude volumes.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties arising from volatile crude prices present an operational challenge.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: Product cracks in international markets declined compared to the previous year.
risks_headwinds.quote: We all know that product cracks have reduced as compared to previous year in the international market, but our endeavor to better the benchmark continues.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL recorded an exchange variation loss of Rs 122 crore in 9M FY2024-25 compared to Rs 72 crore in FY2023-24.
CPCL incurred CST under-recovery of Rs 246 crore during 9M FY2024-25.
CPCL reported a Loss Before Tax of Rs 374 crore for 9M FY2024-25 against a Profit Before Tax of Rs 3,660 crore in FY2023-24.

management_commitments.claim: Management expects commissioning of retail outlets under 300 licenses during FY 2026-27.
management_commitments.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: The combined INR 2,000 crore capex for LOBS and retail projects will be executed over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL projects annual maintenance CAPEX of Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores for each of the next two years.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
